title: OpenUniverse 2D/3D Game Engine
description: I developed a reusable Java game-engine architecture that combined the 2D OpenWorld engine with the JOGL/OpenGL-based 3D OpenGalaxy engine through a higher-level OpenUniverse framework. Both engines used declarative XML scene authoring to construct runtime objects, configure cameras, animation, movement, AI, collision, rendering and other behavior. The 3D engine was ultimately used to build a working client/server two-player kart racing game. This work directly influenced the later FX prototype and Hydra-Gen's declarative presentation architecture.

sections.title: Three-Layer Engine Architecture
paragraphs: The project evolved as a family of related engine layers rather than a single monolithic renderer.
OpenWorld provided the reusable 2D systems, OpenGalaxy provided the reusable 3D systems, and OpenUniverse acted as the higher-level framework connecting the two approaches.
items: OpenGalaxy: 3D JOGL/OpenGL runtime and scene engine
OpenUniverse: higher-level integration and application shell

sections.title: Declarative XML Scene Architecture
paragraphs: A central design goal was to move scene construction and presentation out of hard-coded Java and into external XML.
Runtime classes could be named in XML and instantiated through reflection, allowing scenes to be assembled from reusable engine objects.

sections.title: OpenWorld 2D Engine
paragraphs: OpenWorld implemented the 2D side of the architecture using Java's 2D rendering stack.

sections.title: OpenGalaxy 3D Engine
paragraphs: OpenGalaxy was the 3D half of the system and used JOGL/OpenGL while retaining the same externally authored scene philosophy.

sections.title: 3D Camera System
paragraphs: OpenGalaxy supported several reusable camera behaviors that could be selected and configured through the scene scripts.

sections.title: Models and Geometry
paragraphs: The renderer supported both engine-generated geometry and externally authored 3D assets.

sections.title: Animation
paragraphs: Animation was treated as a reusable engine capability rather than being hard-coded into individual game objects.

sections.title: AI and Movement
paragraphs: The engine contained reusable live-object and NPC abstractions for moving game entities.

sections.title: Collision
paragraphs: Collision support existed on both sides of the engine family, with implementations appropriate to the different rendering environments.

sections.title: Client/Server Networking
paragraphs: The surviving OpenGalaxy code contains an implemented TCP client/server networking system rather than only planned networking hooks.
The engine could operate in NONE, CLIENT or SERVER modes and exchange runtime player state through a network thread.
items: Remote key press and release messages

sections.title: Two-Player Kart Racing Game
paragraphs: I used OpenGalaxy to build a working kart racing game that exercised the engine's scene, camera, model, AI, HUD and networking systems.
The surviving scripts show the race itself being assembled declaratively from player vehicles, opponents, track assets, cameras, lights, skybox, HUD elements and GPS-style markers.

sections.title: 2D and 3D in One Architecture
paragraphs: OpenWorld and OpenGalaxy were separate rendering engines but shared many of the same architectural ideas: reusable runtime objects, externally authored scenes, cameras, animation, movement, AI and collision.
OpenUniverse provided the conceptual and application-level bridge between the 2D OpenWorld and 3D OpenGalaxy systems.

sections.title: Architecture Lineage
paragraphs: The XML-driven architecture became an important precursor to my later FX prototype, which expanded the declarative model into UI layout, data and event binding, animations, code binding and visual effects.
Those experiments subsequently influenced Hydra-Gen's production XML scripting, EWidget, animation and theming systems.

historicalNotes: This was a personal engine project created before Square Particle existed.
It is grouped under the Square Particle umbrella in the modern portfolio to keep Jamie's personal game-engine lineage together.
It was not developed as an Essential Skills project.
Jamie may have reused or adapted a small amount of code from an earlier Essential Skills SE engine, but OpenWorld, OpenGalaxy and OpenUniverse were developed as Jamie's personal engine architecture.
